Invoice approval

LiveEdited by Dana Kowalski, 2 days ago
How it works
  1. Triggerledgerly New bill in Ledgerly Any vendor, any entity
  2. ActionRelaypoint Read invoice fields Vendor, amount, PO number, due date
  3. Condition Amount over $5,000? Or vendor added in the last 30 days
    Yes
    If yesmurmur Ask the controller to approve Reminder after 1 business day
    No
    If noledgerly Match to PO and approve Within 2% of the PO total
  4. Actionledgerly Schedule payment 3 days before the due date
  5. Actionmurmur Post to #ap-daily One summary at 4:00 PM

How it works

  2. Condition Sensitive app? Finance, payroll or customer data
    Yes
    If yesmurmur Manager and app owner approve Both must approve within 3 days
    No
    If nomurmur Manager approves One tap in chat
  3. Actionkeyring Grant access for 90 days Least-privilege role for the app
  4. ActionSheetwise Write to the access log Who asked, who approved, when
  5. Actionmurmur Remind the owner before expiry 7 days before access ends

Security, in plain language

Your IT team will want to know how Relaypoint handles your data before anyone connects a tool. Here are the answers in plain words; the review pack has the detail.

Security review pack for your IT team

  • Architecture and data-flow diagram
  • Data handling and retention summary
  • Completed standard security questionnaire
  • Subprocessor list
  • Incident response summary
Request the review pack
What does Relaypoint store?
The workflow you built, a log of each run, and the fields a step needs to do its job. Attachments like invoice PDFs are passed through, not kept, unless you turn on run archives.
How are connections to our tools protected?
Each connection uses the narrowest permission the tool offers. Credentials are encrypted and never shown again after you connect, not even to admins.
Who at Relaypoint can see our data?
No one by default. If you open a support case, you can grant a named engineer access to one workflow for a set number of hours, and every view is logged.
Can we control who changes workflows?
Yes. Builders edit, approvers only approve, and viewers only read. Every published change keeps a version you can compare and roll back.
How long are run logs kept?
Ninety days by default. You can shorten that to seven days or extend it to two years, per workflow.
What happens if we leave?
Export your workflows and run history as files at any time. When you close the account, your data is deleted within 30 days.

Pay for the runs you use

No per-seat pricing, so the controller, every hiring manager and the whole IT team can approve without you counting licenses. Pick a monthly volume to see an illustrative cost.

  • A run is one trip through a workflow, however many steps it has.
  • Unlimited builders, approvers and viewers.
  • Test runs and failed runs aren't counted.
